name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+12 district with incumbent Brian Babin running for reelection
Fundraising dominance: Babin holds about $928K on hand versus roughly $6K for Hart
Prediction markets price a Democratic upset at only about 5%
No public polls or expert ratings; structural indicators carry the forecast
model.rationale: A twelve-point Republican lean, Babin's roughly fifty-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win at five percent all point to a comfortable incumbent hold; with no polls available, uncertainty stays elevated but the seat remains firmly Republican.
model.watch: New polling showing the race within single digits, or a sudden wave of Democratic outside spending, would be the clearest sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 36th District leans Republican by twelve points, and incumbent Brian Babin is seeking another term with a commanding financial edge. He has raised about $1.2 million and holds roughly $928,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Rhonda Hart has raised about $24,000 with under $6,000 available. No outside spending has been reported on either side, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a five percent chance of an upset, and the district's underlying partisan balance points the same direction. The national political environment offers Democrats some offsetting benefit, but the combination of incumbency, the district lean, and the fundraising gap makes a competitive race unlikely. Babin remains a strong favorite, though the absence of polling means the outlook rests on structural indicators rather than direct measurement of voter opinion.
